title: Detail sections
text: Choose which deeper explanation sections appear below the main summary. You can hide sections you do not need or reorder them for the way you read.

title: Owner/model
text: Hugging Face names model repositories as owner/model. The owner is the account or organisation. The model is the repository name.

title: Hugging Face
text: A large website where people publish AI models, datasets, demos, and documentation. It is powerful, but many pages assume technical background.

title: Model card
text: The README-style explanation for a model. It may describe intended use, limitations, examples, training notes, and licence details.

title: Dataset
text: A collection of examples used for training, testing, or evaluating models. It is not itself a model you run for chat or generation.

title: Space
text: A hosted demo or app on Hugging Face. A Space may use a model, but it is different from a model repository.

title: Collection
text: A curated group of Hugging Face models, datasets, Spaces, or papers. Open an individual model inside the collection for this extension to explain it.

title: Chat template
text: The message format a chat model expects. It tells software where the user, assistant, and system messages go before the model generates an answer.

title: Metadata
text: Structured facts attached to the model page, such as task, licence, tags, files, and update time. Metadata can be incomplete.

title: Repository
text: The model's folder on Hugging Face. It usually contains weights, tokenizer files, config files, and the model card.

title: Pipeline tag
text: A Hugging Face label for the model's likely job, such as text-generation, feature-extraction, or text-to-image.

title: Parameters
text: The learned numbers inside a model. More parameters usually mean larger files and more memory use, but not automatically better results.

title: B model size label
text: In model names, B usually means billion parameters. A 3B model has about 3 billion learned numbers. Bigger models usually need more memory.

title: Quantisation
text: A way to store model weights with fewer bits so they use less disk and memory. It can make local use easier, with possible quality tradeoffs.

title: GGUF
text: A model file format commonly used by local model tools built around llama.cpp, including many beginner desktop workflows.

title: safetensors
text: A common format for storing model weights, often used with Python machine-learning tools.

title: Tokenizer
text: The part that turns text into tokens the model can process, then turns output tokens back into text.

title: Context length
text: How much text the model can consider at once. Longer context can require more memory while the model runs.

title: VRAM
text: Fast memory on a graphics card. Many local model tools use VRAM when available.

title: System RAM
text: The main memory in your computer. Some model setups can use system RAM when the model does not fully fit in VRAM.

title: LM Studio
text: A desktop app that can be beginner-friendly for trying many local language models, especially GGUF models.

title: Ollama
text: A local model runner controlled mainly by commands and a local API. A Hugging Face page does not always map directly to an Ollama model.

title: Python Transformers
text: Hugging Face's Python library for loading and running many models. Powerful, but usually more technical than a desktop app.

title: Gated model
text: A model that may require signing in, accepting terms, or getting approval before files can be downloaded.

title: Licence
text: The rules for using or sharing the model. Missing metadata is not permission; check the original model page for actual terms.

title: Author
text: The Hugging Face account or organisation that published the model repository.

title: Model name
text: The repository name for this model. It may include version, size, tuning style, or format clues.

title: Library
text: The software ecosystem the repository is most likely designed for, such as Transformers, Diffusers, MLX, or another model library.

title: Private model
text: A private model is not publicly accessible. This extension is designed for public model pages.

title: Files
text: The files in the model repository. File names and formats often reveal how the model can be loaded or run.

title: Last modified
text: When Hugging Face reports that the model repository was last updated.

title: Confidence
text: How certain the extension is about an interpretation. High confidence usually means the fact came from structured data or a strong file-name signal.

title: Model type
text: A plain-English category for how the model is likely meant to be used, such as chat, instruct, base, code, embedding, image, audio, reranking, or classification.

title: Architecture
text: The model design or software class used by loading tools. It is useful for developers but can be hard to interpret without context.

title: Detected formats
text: File formats the extension found in the repository, such as GGUF, safetensors, PyTorch, ONNX, or MLX.

title: Detected quantisation
text: Quantisation labels found in file names, tags, or model notes. These labels help estimate memory use.

title: Best target
text: The model size range the extension thinks is the most sensible starting point for the saved hardware profile and selected goal.

title: Stretch target
text: A larger or more demanding option that might work, but is more likely to be slow, tight, or require extra setup.

title: Local only
text: Prefer models and file formats that are practical to run on your own computer instead of relying on hosted inference.

title: Permissive licence
text: A licence that usually allows broad reuse, often including Apache-2.0 or MIT. Always check the model page before relying on this.

title: Find a Model for Me
text: A guided search helper that turns your goal, hardware profile, and preferences into a safer starting point on Hugging Face.

title: Rank by
text: How the extension chooses a starting candidate from Hugging Face search results. Downloads and likes are popularity signals, not guarantees.

title: Size preference
text: Whether the search should lean toward faster smaller models, stronger larger models, or a balance between the two.

title: Search priority
text: Fields higher in Find a Model for Me matter more when the extension chooses between candidate models. Use the arrows to move a field higher or lower.

title: Downloads and likes
text: Popularity signals from Hugging Face. They can help find active models, but they do not prove a model is safe, high quality, or right for your computer.

title: Evaluation benchmark
text: A test used to compare model performance. Benchmarks are useful clues, but they do not guarantee the model is right for your task or computer.

title: Hardware fit
text: A cautious estimate of whether the model can run on the saved hardware profile. It is not a guarantee.

title: Hardware profile
text: The computer specs the extension uses for local-run estimates, especially GPU VRAM and system RAM.

title: Operating system
text: The main software your computer runs, such as Windows, macOS, or Linux. Some local AI tools work differently depending on this.

title: Experience level
text: How comfortable you are with technical setup. Beginner settings favour desktop tools and simpler next steps.

title: Bits per parameter
text: How many bits are used to store each learned number in the model. Lower values usually mean smaller memory use.

title: Weight memory
text: An estimate of memory used by the model weights alone, before extra runtime overhead.

title: Runtime range
text: A cautious estimate of memory while the model is actually running, including overhead beyond the weight files.

title: Recommended tool
text: The route that currently looks most practical from the model type, file formats, and saved hardware profile.

title: Commands
text: Example commands are shown only when the extension has enough verified information to avoid misleading the learner.

title: GPU
text: A graphics processor. GPUs can make local AI models much faster when the model fits in VRAM.

title: CPU
text: The main processor in your computer. Some local models can run on CPU, but usually more slowly than on a GPU.

title: GB
text: Gigabytes, a common unit for memory and file size.

title: Tokens
text: Pieces of text processed by a model. A token can be a word, part of a word, punctuation, or spacing.

title: FP16
text: A 16-bit number format often used for model weights. It uses less memory than FP32 but more than many quantised formats.

title: BF16
text: A 16-bit number format common in modern machine learning. It has similar storage size to FP16 with different numeric behavior.

title: FP32
text: A 32-bit number format. It is larger in memory than FP16, BF16, or quantised model files.

title: INT8
text: An 8-bit integer format or quantisation level that can reduce memory use compared with 16-bit or 32-bit weights.

title: GGUF quantisation label
text: A compact label for how much the model weights were compressed. Lower-bit labels usually use less memory, with possible quality tradeoffs.

title: PyTorch
text: A popular machine-learning framework. PyTorch model files usually point toward a Python-based workflow.

title: ONNX
text: A model format designed for ONNX Runtime and compatible tools. It is usually more developer-oriented than beginner desktop apps.

title: MLX
text: Apple's machine-learning framework. MLX model files are mainly relevant to Apple silicon workflows.

title: API
text: A way for software to request data from another service. This extension uses the public Hugging Face API for model metadata.

title: Filtered Search
text: Opens Hugging Face model search in a new tab using the goal and filters selected here. Use it when you want to browse beyond the suggested starting candidate.

title: Browse Small Local Models
text: Opens a narrower Hugging Face search in a new tab for smaller or compressed model variants that are more likely to suit local beginner tools.
